**My thinking:**

I have been working this land for 30 years. I know what grows here in Quzhou and what the market will take. Some of my children work in the city now, so I cannot rely on as many hands as before. I keep to what I know.

My 8 mu breaks down simply: 6 mu goes to the wheat-maize rotation — that is my stable income and food for the family. The other 2 mu I split between cotton and watermelon, both cash crops I have grown for years. Watermelon sells well locally in summer. Cotton takes work but the price has held up.

For wheat I use the improved variety that the village has been using for years — not the newest hybrid, which costs more and I am not sure about. I apply base fertilizer before planting and top-dress at jointing. I will irrigate in winter to protect roots from frost, again at jointing, and at heading — three times is usually enough with my well. For summer maize I go straight to hybrid seed because the yield difference is real and I have seen it myself. I plant no-till right after wheat harvest to save time and moisture. Two or three irrigations depending on how the summer rain goes.

For cotton I plough properly in spring. It needs more pesticide attention — bollworm especially — but I know the schedule. I irrigate more because cotton roots go deep and it suffers in dry spells. For watermelon, I rotate it on the 1 mu I used for watermelon last year — actually I need to move it to avoid fusarium, so I will put it on a different plot this year.
